title: Conclusions Practice 1
description: 4 short texts - 8 conclusion and generalization questions
subject: rla
passage:
TEXT A - Tool Lending

A library added evening pickup hours for borrowed tools. Evening pickups increased, and fewer reservations expired before collection. Staff time also increased slightly because one employee stayed later.

TEXT B - Classroom Plants

Three classrooms added identical plants. Two classes assigned a weekly watering schedule and kept most plants healthy. The third had no schedule and lost several plants after repeated missed watering.

TEXT C - Reading Nook

A school added a small reading nook near a busy hallway. Students used it often, but hallway noise made concentration difficult. After acoustic dividers were installed, use stayed high and students reported fewer distractions.

TEXT D - Volunteer Training

New volunteers either attended one long lecture or completed three shorter sessions with practice between them. Both groups learned the rules, but the short-session group made fewer procedural errors during the first month.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is best supported by Text A?
questions.explanation: It combines the benefit and the staffing tradeoff.
questions.rule: Synthesize the pattern, then keep the conclusion within the evidence.

options.text: Keeping the library open later would eliminate expired reservations entirely.
options.whyWrong: “Keeping the library open later would eliminate expired reservations entirely.” is broader or more absolute than the passage supports.

options.text: The increase in staff time proves evening pickup was not worthwhile.
options.whyWrong: “The increase in staff time proves evening pickup was not worthwhile.” turns limited evidence into a broader rule than the text supports.

options.text: Evening pickup improved collection outcomes but required some additional staffing time.
Evening pickup increased because one employee stayed later.
options.whyWrong: “Evening pickup increased because one employee stayed later.” reverses the relationship established by the passage.
